definition: A website that hosts git repositories, allowing you to share code and collaborate with others.
A version of your repository that is hosted on the internet or another network, like GitHub.
Upload your local commits to a remote repository.
Download a full copy of a remote repository onto your computer.
Download new commits from the remote repository and merge them into your local branch.
A file named README.md that tells people what a project is. Hosting sites show it on the repo page.
The usual nickname for the main copy of a project online. It is a habit, not a rule.
The branch online that your local branch is linked to. Set it once with git push -u.
Download new commits from online without changing your own files.
A pointer that remembers where main was online the last time you looked. Fetch moves it.
Git refuses a push when the copy online has commits you do not have. Pull first, then push again.
